findings.finding: A1: 'The previous release' is undefined; production pins an image, tags are cut for some paths, CI has no history, a previous build below 0117 fails by design.
findings.answer: Plan 0.4/G1/G5: the previous build is a commit built from source with git archive; CI default is the newest legion-envoy-v* tag that is an ancestor of the PR base, with fetch-depth 0; a workflow_dispatch input takes any commit; the script refuses a commit below migration 0117. The INFRA-63 architect answered (Envoy, 02:45Z) that INFRA-564's spec runs the harness with the commit production ran before the measured release.

findings.finding: A2: Leniency protects only once a lenient build is the previous one; sibling children adding request members in the same window are refused by the strict build.
findings.answer: The INFRA-63 architect answered (Envoy, 02:45Z): INFRA-561 raises the server count only onto a build carrying INFRA-558 and INFRA-559 on every pod. Plan 0.3 and departure 3: this release adds no request member.

findings.finding: A3: Meaning search on new-identity pods during an embedder roll returns no vector hits.
findings.answer: Plan E-a and departure 2: accepted as text-only matches on the inactive identity, the same gap a one-process embedder change has today; README says so; dual vectors need a new embeddings layout (one row per (kind,id), vector(1536)).

findings.finding: B1: Admission by |client-server|<=1 can admit a stale tab writable and let y-prosemirror delete an element; nothing separates readable from creatable; corpus cross-read is Go-only.
findings.answer: Plan D2/D3/D5: per-element since/creatable_since in the manifest; write paths refuse elements not yet creatable; admission writable iff R_client <= min V of the live fleet and C_client >= max(fleet R, elements present in the document); sockets re-checked every 30 s. G4's browser half checks the page side across builds.

findings.finding: B2: pending-sync may replay a y-prosemirror deletion recorded while read-only.
findings.answer: Plan D9: a web test on the pinned versions; if the editor deletes, exclude its repair transactions from the pending store and never send them from a read-only socket; acceptance is the element surviving a read-only session followed by a writable admission.

findings.finding: B3: Writing no version when the approved version is unreadable can block settlement forever, including for versions an earlier release stored.
findings.answer: Plan D7: applies to the newer-content class (D6) only; skipUnreadableVersion stays for versions an earlier release stored.

findings.finding: B4: Leaving unreadable documents owed starves the excerpt batch (from_id order, limit 20).
findings.answer: Plan D8: newer-content class only, plus a per-process skip set keyed by artifact and version so the batch moves past them; test reconciles a 26th normal document past 25 unreadable ones.

findings.finding: B5: A composite duty_passes key doubles passes during this release's own roll at equal periods.
findings.answer: Plan E-c: the new build also reads the legacy lease=name row when its period_ns equals its own, and writes it only when absent or at its own period.

findings.finding: B6: The two embedder takeover rules contradict each other.
findings.answer: Plan E-a: one rule, stored in a singleton embedder_active row: the active identity stays active while any live process carries it; then the earliest-started live process's identity takes over by compare-and-set.

findings.finding: B7: Registry and holds protect only builds that carry them; takeover could steal from a pre-change holder that never rebinds.
findings.answer: Plan 0.3 and F1: protections bind from the release after the first carrying them; this release changes no setting. Plan A1: rows of builds before INFRA-558 (registry defaults) are left out of fleet numbers and treated as lacking the bucket. Plan C5: a new build never takes a binding from a deliver subject no lease recorded; it waits until that consumer is unbound.

findings.finding: B8: Stream Metadata cannot protect against the previous build; preserving Replicas would change ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS; usesCoreTransport is shared with the listener and outbox.
findings.answer: Plan C1: MaxAge/Duplicates/Subjects unchanged this release. Plan C2: only a client without WithReplicas (Dispatch) keeps deployed Replicas; the listener's meaning is unchanged. Plan C4 and 'Coordination': the shared transport change is told to INFRA-557 and INFRA-514; outbox code untouched.

findings.finding: B9: /api/v1/schema/blocks must stay and stay readable by old tabs; new keys outside types.
findings.answer: Plan D2: endpoint unchanged byte for byte; nodes and marks are new top-level keys; per-element since fields are keys the previous validateBlockSchema ignores (read at legion-envoy-v18.1.0 block-schema.ts:51-70).

findings.finding: C1-C2: The claim route's trust comment and the daemon's strict-text ride-out and labels_add probe test depend on strictness.
findings.answer: Plan B3: comments rewritten; daemon ride-out left as is (right against strict builds; both fields known at legion-envoy-v18.1.0); api/issues_test.go:701-708 probes by effect; README rule says a future precondition ships as a route.

findings.finding: C3-C4: New enum values (view.kind, ?kind=, cursor) and response members are not unknown fields.
findings.answer: Plan B2/B6 (view kind degrades and the page reconnects), D11 (?kind= answers unknown_kinds), F1 (cursors and response members reader-first / optional).

findings.finding: C5: A new document error class reaches contracts, generated Go, tool descriptions, plugin bundles, web, README and AGENTS docs.
findings.answer: Plan D6 lists each consumer, the new close code (verified against the pinned Hocuspocus provider), and the web state.

findings.finding: C6-C7: 0117 note; migration numbers may collide.
findings.answer: Plan F1 keeps 0113/0117 as history and the one-time 0117 stop; 'Coordination' says the later PR renumbers.

findings.answer: Real browser via Playwright (G4) in its own CI job; SIGKILL covered with a 25 s bound (C5); all four document messages stop giving destructive advice (D6); turning the store off needs restore-files first (E-b, F1); retry then message (B4/B5).

findings.answer: Plan G3 negative control via ENVOY_TEST_GO_OVERLAY; numbers in C5 (5 s, 25 s) and E; equal sets of event and delivery ids in G2; items 5 and 6 named as having none; document fails-before comes from single-build tests with a synthetic element (D3, D6).

findings.answer: D9 and D6 verify the pinned libraries; B7 adds a router test for the wrong-method answer; the CLI fallback is kept (B5).

Plan 'Coordination', following the INFRA-63 architect's answer (02:45Z): A1 adds columns to INFRA-555's server_processes (no registry of our own); A2 shares one holder lease with INFRA-514 (asked its architect, message b7221345c44cbae099529670069b2625); G4 extends INFRA-559's two-process browser harness (no harness of our own); INFRA-557 told of the shared bus code; Document-rooms finding 8 stays here (D5).

findings.finding: H: Tests skip without Postgres in a pod; CI needs history; previous build must be >=0117.
findings.answer: Plan H: failing-before shown on CI with test-only commits, or locally with the documented rootless Postgres under $TMPDIR; G5 fetch-depth 0; G1 refuses below 0117 (tag 18.1.0 carries through 0120).

findings.finding: Architect (Envoy, 02:45Z) via INFRA-557's planner: nats-server refuses to change a push consumer's deliver subject while the old subject has interest, which a dead connection keeps for 2-4 minutes, so rotation fails when fencing is needed.
findings.answer: Plan C5 deletes and recreates the durable at AckFloor+1 with a fresh deliver subject; the interest check applies only to a config update (nats-server v2.10.29 server/consumer.go:1873-1883), not to a delete or a create on a new subject; the intake already deletes and recreates at the ack floor (intake.go:607-614). Each holder handles a message only while it holds the lease.

specDepartures.spec: Item 2: a build reads and edits documents containing elements written by the other build without refusing them.
specDepartures.plan: Elements become creatable one release after they are readable (manifest since/creatable_since, write-path refusal, fleet admission), so the other build only writes elements this build reads; an element a build does not know is refused with a non-destructive retry error (DOC_NEWER_CONTENT), never read opaquely.
specDepartures.evidence: y-prosemirror deletes a Yjs element its schema cannot build (upstream sync-plugin.js createNodeFromYElement; pinned copy verified in task D9); Markdown has no form for an unknown node or mark; pmdoc validateNode is the one gate for read, parse, render and write (pmdoc/node.go:101).

specDepartures.spec: Item 4: releases that change embedder settings work while both builds serve, by a change to the code.
specDepartures.plan: The builds stop undoing each other (one active identity in the database; the inactive identity neither drops nor embeds), and meaning search on a process of the inactive identity returns text matches only until the active identity changes.
specDepartures.evidence: A query is embedded with the serving process's identity and matched with e.model = that identity (api/search.go:228-481); embeddings holds one vector per (kind, id), vector(1536) (migration 0072), so two identities cannot be covered at once without a new layout.

specDepartures.spec: Outcome: two builds serve together 'for every release'.
specDepartures.plan: Every protection (lenient decoding, generations, registry, holds) binds from the release after the first one carrying it; this release changes no request member, document element, stream or consumer setting, embedder or file store default, or loop interval, because the previous build would refuse or revert it.
specDepartures.evidence: The previous build decodes strictly (api/server.go:833), compares stream and consumer settings without generations (bus/stream.go:271-300, delivery/intake.go:618-635), and neither registers nor holds.

summary: 'for every release' holds from the release after the one that deploys this change; that first overlap is protected only where the strict previous build already behaves.
